items.followUp: What is the organ level of biological organization?

rubric.why: Identifies that an organ system consists of cooperating organs.
rubric.description: Organs work together as a unit.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that organs work or cooperate together.

rubric.why: Explains the system’s role or gives a relevant example.
rubric.description: The organs perform a particular major function; a suitable example may be given.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the function idea or a correct example.

modelAnswer: An organ system is a group of organs that work together to perform a particular major function.
For example, the digestive system consists of organs that work together to digest food.

items.followUp: Name a Muslim scientist who made an important contribution to the study of animals.

rubric.why: Correctly identifies the scientist associated with the study of animals.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct name.

rubric.why: Gives his contribution to animal studies.
rubric.description: States that he studied animals or wrote the Book of Animals.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct contribution.

modelAnswer: Al-Jahiz was a Muslim scientist who studied animals.
He wrote Kitab-ul-Haywan (The Book of Animals).

items.followUp: Define biometry and state what it applies to.

rubric.why: Identifies the quantitative methods used in biometry.
rubric.description: Biometry uses mathematical or statistical methods.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for mentioning mathematics or statistics.

rubric.why: Identifies the field to which those methods are applied.
rubric.description: The methods are applied to biological phenomena or research.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for linking the methods to biology.

modelAnswer: Biometry is the application of mathematical and statistical methods to biological phenomena.
It is used in biological research.

items.followUp: What is the incubation period of an infectious disease?

rubric.why: Identifies the period as beginning after infection.
rubric.description: It is a time interval following infection or entry of a pathogen.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the interval after infection.

rubric.why: Identifies the event that ends the period.
rubric.description: The period ends when symptoms appear.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for mentioning the appearance of symptoms.

modelAnswer: The incubation period is the time between the entry of a pathogen into the body and the appearance of the disease symptoms.

items.followUp: State four characteristics of a good hypothesis.

rubric.why: A hypothesis must be a reasoned, provisional explanation that can be checked.
rubric.description: Gives any two valid characteristics, such as testable, tentative, logical, or based on observations.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for any two distinct valid characteristics.

rubric.why: Rewards further correct characteristics from the requested four.
rubric.description: Gives two further valid characteristics of a hypothesis.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for two further distinct characteristics; do not credit a characteristic already counted.

modelAnswer: A hypothesis is a tentative explanation based on observations.
It should be logical and testable.
It can be accepted or rejected after testing.
It should be supported by evidence.

items.followUp: How is a scientific law established? Give one example.

rubric.why: States that repeated testing provides support for the scientific statement.
rubric.description: The proposed explanation or pattern is tested repeatedly and supported by evidence.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for repeated testing or experiments with supporting evidence.

rubric.why: Provides a valid example of a scientific law.
rubric.description: Gives one example, such as Mendel’s law of segregation.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct example.

modelAnswer: In the textbook’s simplified account, a theory that is repeatedly tested and supported by evidence is stated as a scientific law.
An example is Mendel’s law of segregation.

items.followUp: What happens when a lysosome fuses with a food vacuole?

rubric.why: Describes what the lysosome contributes to the vacuole.
rubric.description: Lysosomal digestive enzymes enter or are released into the vacuole.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the release or entry of digestive enzymes.

rubric.why: States the result of the fusion.
rubric.description: The enzymes digest the vacuole’s contents, carrying out intracellular digestion.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for digestion of the vacuole contents.

modelAnswer: The lysosome releases its digestive enzymes into the vacuole.
These enzymes digest the vacuole’s contents, resulting in intracellular digestion.

items.followUp: What is taxonomy, and how is it related to systematics?

rubric.why: Identifies the main activities of taxonomy.
rubric.description: Taxonomy deals with identification, naming, and classification of organisms.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming a relevant taxonomic activity.

rubric.why: Explains the broader scope of systematics and its relation to taxonomy.
rubric.description: Taxonomy is part of systematics; systematics also considers relationships among organisms, including evolutionary relationships.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating the relationship or the broader scope of systematics.

modelAnswer: Taxonomy deals with the identification, naming, and classification of organisms.
It is a part of systematics, which also studies relationships among organisms, including their evolutionary relationships.
